entries.arrival_reason: A person arrives where the starter's snapshot states its spawn, and the society reads that point from the world: nobody starts on it or within 2,000 mm of it, and a successor that moves it is refused.
entries.floor_reason: The starter's own ground module states the ground people stand on, and the app draws it; the society reads it and declares nothing more to stand on.
entries.population_reason: A society on this ground starts with eight people. Its area is a square about 23 metres across with 121 places to stand, and a population sized for a district (128) would stand people on top of each other from the first minute; a handful reads as people living somewhere. Eight is also what one comparison of models runs (the comparison protocol's population_maximum), so every society made here can be compared.
entries.lattice_reason: People route over a square lattice at this spacing. A flat ground has no paths of its own, so a route graph over it is a choice this entry makes rather than a fact the world states. Two metres keeps every point of the area within 1,415 mm of a lattice node, which is inside the reviewed object reach, and keeps a 24 m area at 121 nodes and 220 edges. Every stored input records the spacing it was composed with, so another figure is a new navigation profile, never an edit of this one.
entries.declared_area_reason: Where the ground states no edge (the endless plane every new starter uses), the society declares a square of this half extent about the region origin and says in its input that it did; the stored world stays endless. The figure keeps the lattice at 121 nodes, which holds one tick of 128 people near a tenth of a second, and it equals the only bounded starter ground the product has shipped, so an old and a new starter give a society the same area and the same node identities.
entries.reason: The ground of a saved world made from the built-in starter: a flat authored region whose society walks a lattice over the area the ground states or, where it states none, the area declared here. Read by the society's ground builder, which composes over it, and by the repository, which starts a society over it with this population.

entries.arrival_reason: A world made from photographs states no spawn and places no region, so the society takes the origin of the region its people live in as where a person arrives. The rule needs nothing authored per world: every region has an origin, the frame the society's lattice and every placed object are measured in, and the same rule holds for every made world. Nothing in the world states another point to prefer.
entries.floor_reason: A made world states no ground, so every one of its regions has a floor the society declares: a square of the declared half extent about the region origin at height 0 in its frame. The app draws it as a floor in every region, so a person sees what people and placed objects stand on, and furniture and the small square can be placed on it where nothing was reconstructed.
entries.population_reason: Eight people, as on the starter's ground: a made world's region states no extent, so its society declares the same 24 m square and walks the same lattice (navigation profile authored-ground-lattice/v1), and the figure that suits that area suits it here. It is also what one comparison of models runs, so a made world's society can be compared.
entries.lattice_reason: The same two metre lattice as the starter's navigation profile, which this ground shares: every point of the area within 1,415 mm of a node, inside the reviewed object reach. A navigation profile names one discretisation, so a ground that shares it states the same figures, and the catalog refuses one that does not.
entries.declared_area_reason: A made world states no ground, so the society declares a square of this half extent about the region origin, the area the starter's lattice and population were measured over. Photographs in the region are drawn without collision, so they do not narrow it; an object placed outside it is still in the world and its activity is recorded as unreachable.
entries.reason: The region of a world made from a person's photographs, which states no ground, no spawn and no position: a society stands in one of its regions, named when people are brought in, and walks a declared area about that region's origin. Read by the society's ground builder, which dispatches on the snapshot's composer, and by the repository through the navigation profile the input records.
